        - generic [ref=f7e93]: "Artisan builds AI employees for revenue teams. Our first, Ava, is the leading AI BDR: she finds and researches leads across a database of 400M+ contacts, writes and sends personalized email in your tone of voice, runs dialer call steps, handles every reply, and books meetings on the right rep's calendar. Over 90% of our customers run her fully autonomously. Artisan is a complete GTM ecosystem, not a point tool. One platform consolidates the 5-8 tool stack most teams stitch together at $100K+/year: prospecting data and waterfall enrichment (ZoomInfo, Apollo), list building and signals (Clay), sequencing (Outreach, Salesloft), parallel dialing (Nooks, Orum), website visitor identification, and buyer intent. Beyond the BDR job, Ava Inbound qualifies and books website visitors from the same knowledge base, and our AI AE runs live product demos and progresses deals. Prospecting, inbound, and the demo on one platform, one knowledge base, one AI sales team. YC W24. $35M+ raised from investors including Y Combinator and HubSpot Ventures.         - generic [ref=f7e93]: "Artisan builds AI employees for revenue teams. Our first, Ava, is the leading AI BDR: she finds and researches leads across a database of 400M+ contacts, writes and sends personalized email in your tone of voice, runs dialer call steps, handles every reply, and books meetings on the right rep's calendar. Over 90% of our customers run her fully autonomously. Artisan is a complete GTM ecosystem, not a point tool. One platform consolidates the 5-8 tool stack most teams stitch together at $100K+/year: prospecting data and waterfall enrichment (ZoomInfo, Apollo), list building and signals (Clay), sequencing (Outreach, Salesloft), parallel dialing (Nooks, Orum), website visitor identification, and buyer intent. It runs on top of Salesforce and HubSpot with owner mapping, do-not-contact enforcement, and field-level sync controls. We're built for enterprise. SOC 2 Type II, GDPR and CCPA compliant, SSO/SAML, role-based access, workspace isolation per brand, and a full audit trail on everything Ava does. The common enterprise pattern: sales ops runs Ava centrally for a thousand-plus AEs who never log in. Beyond the BDR job, Ava Inbound qualifies and books website visitors from the same knowledge base, and our AI AE runs live product demos and progresses deals. Prospecting, inbound, and the demo on one platform, one knowledge base, one AI sales team. YC W24. $35M+ raised from investors including Y Combinator and HubSpot Ventures. Thousands of customers including DoorDash, Quora, SumUp, CookUnity and SaaStr. Raise sourced over $700K in ARR in six months with Ava. SumUp runs leads at $52 each. Teams in San Francisco and New York. And we're hiring."

        - generic [ref=f7e93]: "Artisan builds AI employees for revenue teams. Our first, Ava, is the leading AI BDR: she finds and researches leads across a database of 400M+ contacts, writes and sends personalized email in your tone of voice, runs dialer call steps, handles every reply, and books meetings on the right rep's calendar. Over 90% of our customers run her fully autonomously. Artisan is a complete GTM ecosystem, not a point tool. One platform consolidates the 5-8 tool stack most teams stitch together at $100K+/year: prospecting data and waterfall enrichment (ZoomInfo, Apollo), list building and signals (Clay), sequencing (Outreach, Salesloft), parallel dialing (Nooks, Orum), website visitor identification, and buyer intent. It runs on top of Salesforce and HubSpot with owner mapping, do-not-contact enforcement, and field-level sync controls. We're built for enterprise. SOC 2 Type II, GDPR and CCPA compliant, SSO/SAML, role-based access, workspace isolation per brand, and a full audit trail on everything Ava does. The common enterprise pattern: sales ops runs Ava centrally for a thousand-plus AEs who never log in. Beyond the BDR job, Ava Inbound qualifies and books website visitors from the same knowledge base, and our AI AE runs live product demos and progresses deals. Prospecting, inbound, and the demo on one platform, one knowledge base, one AI sales team. YC W24. $35M+ raised from investors including Y Combinator and HubSpot Ventures. Thousands of customers including DoorDash, Quora, SumUp, CookUnity and SaaStr. Raise sourced over $700K in ARR in six months with Ava. SumUp runs leads at $52 each. Teams in San Francisco and New York. And we're hiring."

                  - text: Graphiti helps you create and query graphs that evolve over time. Think of a knowledge graph as a network of interconnected facts, such as

                  - text: ), and their relationship, or edge (
                  - emphasis [ref=f8e138]: ”loves”
                  - text: ). Knowledge Graphs have been explored extensively for information retrieval. What makes Graphiti unique is its ability to autonomously build a knowledge graph while handling changing relationships and maintaining historical context.

                  - text: At Zep, we build a

                  - text: . Developers use Zep to recall relevant user information from past conversations without including the entire chat history in a prompt. Accurate context is crucial for LLM applications. If an AI agent doesn't remember that you've changed jobs or confuses the chronology of events, its responses can be jarring or irrelevant, or worse, inaccurate.
                - heading "Zep’s Suboptimal Fact Pipeline" [level=1] [ref=f8e141]
                - paragraph [ref=f8e142]: Before Graphiti, our approach to storing and retrieving user “memory” was, in effect, a specialized RAG pipeline. An LLM extracted “facts” from a user’s chat history. Semantic search, reranking, and other techniques then surfaced facts relevant to the current conversation back to a developer for inclusion in their prompt.
                - paragraph [ref=f8e143]: Unfortunately, this approach became problematic. Reconciling facts from increasingly complex conversations challenged even frontier LLMs such as gpt-4o. We saw incomplete facts, poor recall, and hallucinations. Our RAG search also failed at times to capture the nuanced relationships between facts, leading to irrelevant or contradictory information being retrieved.
                - paragraph [ref=f8e144]: We tried fixing these issues with prompt optimization but saw diminishing returns on effort. We realized that a graph would help model a user’s complex world, potentially addressing these challenges.
                - heading "Building Graphiti" [level=1] [ref=f8e145]
                - paragraph [ref=f8e146]: "We were intrigued by Microsoft’s GraphRAG, which expanded on RAG text chunking with a graph to better model a document corpus. However, it didn't solve our core problem: GraphRAG is designed for static documents and doesn't natively handle temporality."

                  - text: So, we built Graphiti, a

                  - listitem [ref=f8e154]:

                  - listitem [ref=f8e156]:
                    - strong [ref=f8e157]: Hybrid Search

                  - listitem [ref=f8e158]:
                    - strong [ref=f8e159]: Scalable
                    - text: ": Designed for large datasets, parallelizing LLM calls for batch processing while preserving event chronology."
                  - listitem [ref=f8e160]:

        - generic [ref=f7e93]: "Artisan builds AI employees for revenue teams. Our first, Ava, is the leading AI BDR: she finds and researches leads across a database of 400M+ contacts, writes and sends personalized email in your tone of voice, runs dialer call steps, handles every reply, and books meetings on the right rep's calendar. Over 90% of our customers run her fully autonomously. Artisan is a complete GTM ecosystem, not a point tool. One platform consolidates the 5-8 tool stack most teams stitch together at $100K+/year: prospecting data and waterfall enrichment (ZoomInfo, Apollo), list building and signals (Clay), sequencing (Outreach, Salesloft), parallel dialing (Nooks, Orum), website visitor identification, and buyer intent. It runs on top of Salesforce and HubSpot with owner mapping, do-not-contact enforcement, and field-level sync controls. We're built for enterprise. SOC 2 Type II, GDPR and CCPA compliant, SSO/SAML, role-based access, workspace isolation per brand, and a full audit trail on everything Ava does. The common enterprise pattern: sales ops runs Ava centrally for a thousand-plus AEs who never log in. Beyond the BDR job, Ava Inbound qualifies and books website visitors from the same knowledge base, and our AI AE runs live product demos and progresses deals. Prospecting, inbound, and the demo on one platform, one knowledge base, one AI sales team. YC W24. $35M+ raised from investors including Y Combinator and HubSpot Ventures. Thousands of customers including DoorDash, Quora, SumUp, CookUnity and SaaStr. Raise sourced over $700K in ARR in six months with Ava. SumUp runs leads at $52 each. Teams in San Francisco and New York. And we're hiring."

          - generic [ref=f8e119]: Company Launches

                - link "See original launch post" [ref=f8e124]:
                  - /url: /launches/Lmc-graphiti-by-zep-ai-a-library-for-building-dynamic-knowledge-graphs
              - generic [ref=f8e128]:
                - paragraph [ref=f8e129]:
                  - text: Hey! We're Paul, Preston, and Daniel from Zep AI. We've just
                  - link "open-sourced Graphiti" [ref=f8e130]:
                    - /url: https://git.new/graphiti
                  - text: ", a Python library for building temporal Knowledge Graphs using LLMs."
                - paragraph [ref=f8e131]:

                                - link "Zep AI" [ref=f9e22] [cursor=pointer]:

                              - generic [ref=f9e24]:
                                - button [ref=f9e25] [cursor=pointer]

                                - generic [ref=f9e43]: Watch on
                - paragraph [ref=f8e135]:
                  - text: Graphiti helps you create and query graphs that evolve over time. Think of a knowledge graph as a network of interconnected facts, such as
                  - emphasis [ref=f8e136]: “Kendra loves Adidas shoes.”
                  - text: Each fact is a “triplet, represented by two entities, or nodes (
                  - emphasis [ref=f8e137]: ”Kendra,” “Adidas shoes”
                  - text: ), and their relationship, or edge (
                  - emphasis [ref=f8e138]: ”loves”
                  - text: ). Knowledge Graphs have been explored extensively for information retrieval. What makes Graphiti unique is its ability to autonomously build a knowledge graph while handling changing relationships and maintaining historical context.
                - paragraph [ref=f8e139]:
                  - text: At Zep, we build a
                  - link "memory layer for LLM applications" [ref=f8e140]:
                    - /url: https://www.getzep.com
                  - text: . Developers use Zep to recall relevant user information from past conversations without including the entire chat history in a prompt. Accurate context is crucial for LLM applications. If an AI agent doesn't remember that you've changed jobs or confuses the chronology of events, its responses can be jarring or irrelevant, or worse, inaccurate.
                - heading "Zep’s Suboptimal Fact Pipeline" [level=1] [ref=f8e141]
                - paragraph [ref=f8e142]: Before Graphiti, our approach to storing and retrieving user “memory” was, in effect, a specialized RAG pipeline. An LLM extracted “facts” from a user’s chat history. Semantic search, reranking, and other techniques then surfaced facts relevant to the current conversation back to a developer for inclusion in their prompt.
                - paragraph [ref=f8e143]: Unfortunately, this approach became problematic. Reconciling facts from increasingly complex conversations challenged even frontier LLMs such as gpt-4o. We saw incomplete facts, poor recall, and hallucinations. Our RAG search also failed at times to capture the nuanced relationships between facts, leading to irrelevant or contradictory information being retrieved.
                - paragraph [ref=f8e144]: We tried fixing these issues with prompt optimization but saw diminishing returns on effort. We realized that a graph would help model a user’s complex world, potentially addressing these challenges.
                - heading "Building Graphiti" [level=1] [ref=f8e145]
                - paragraph [ref=f8e146]: "We were intrigued by Microsoft’s GraphRAG, which expanded on RAG text chunking with a graph to better model a document corpus. However, it didn't solve our core problem: GraphRAG is designed for static documents and doesn't natively handle temporality."
                - paragraph [ref=f8e147]:
                  - img "uploaded image" [ref=f8e148]
                - paragraph [ref=f8e149]:
                  - text: So, we built Graphiti, a
                  - link "temporal Knowledge Graph" [ref=f8e150]:
                    - /url: https://github.com/getzep/graphiti
                  - text: "library, which is designed from the ground up to handle constantly changing information, hybrid semantic and graph search, and scale:"
                - list [ref=f8e151]:
                  - listitem [ref=f8e152]:
                    - strong [ref=f8e153]: Temporal Awareness
                    - text: ": Tracks changes in facts and relationships over time. Graph edges include temporal metadata to record relationship lifecycles."
                  - listitem [ref=f8e154]:
                    - strong [ref=f8e155]: Episodic Processing
                    - text: ": Ingests data as discrete episodes, maintaining data provenance and enabling incremental processing."
                  - listitem [ref=f8e156]:
                    - strong [ref=f8e157]: Hybrid Search
                    - text: ": Semantic and BM25 full-text search, with the ability to rerank results by distance from a central node."
                  - listitem [ref=f8e158]:
                    - strong [ref=f8e159]: Scalable
                    - text: ": Designed for large datasets, parallelizing LLM calls for batch processing while preserving event chronology."
                  - listitem [ref=f8e160]:
                    - strong [ref=f8e161]: Varied Sources
                    - text: ": Ingests both unstructured text and structured data."
                - heading "Getting Started" [level=1] [ref=f8e162]
                - paragraph [ref=f8e163]:
                  - text: "Graphiti is open-source and available on GitHub:"
                  - link "https://git.new/graphiti" [ref=f8e164]:
                    - /url: https://git.new/graphiti
                - paragraph [ref=f8e165]:
                  - text: "Quick Start:"
                  - code [ref=f8e166]: "`pip install graphiti-core`"
                - paragraph [ref=f8e167]: "While we developed Graphiti for our needs at Zep, we believe it could be useful for any application dealing with evolving, interconnected data, such as:"
                - list [ref=f8e168]:
                  - listitem [ref=f8e169]: Personal AI assistants that need to maintain user context over time
                  - listitem [ref=f8e170]: Knowledge management systems for rapidly changing domains
                  - listitem [ref=f8e171]: Social network analysis tools
                  - listitem [ref=f8e172]: Financial systems tracking changing relationships and transactions
                - paragraph [ref=f8e173]: If you try, we'd love to hear your thoughts, questions, and experiences. Please also consider contributing!

                - paragraph [ref=f8e135]:
                  - text: Graphiti helps you create and query graphs that evolve over time. Think of a knowledge graph as a network of interconnected facts, such as
                  - emphasis [ref=f8e136]: “Kendra loves Adidas shoes.”
                  - text: Each fact is a “triplet, represented by two entities, or nodes (
                  - emphasis [ref=f8e137]: ”Kendra,” “Adidas shoes”
                  - text: ), and their relationship, or edge (
                  - emphasis [ref=f8e138]: ”loves”
                  - text: ). Knowledge Graphs have been explored extensively for information retrieval. What makes Graphiti unique is its ability to autonomously build a knowledge graph while handling changing relationships and maintaining historical context.
                - paragraph [ref=f8e139]:
                  - text: At Zep, we build a
                  - link "memory layer for LLM applications" [ref=f8e140]:
                    - /url: https://www.getzep.com
                  - text: . Developers use Zep to recall relevant user information from past conversations without including the entire chat history in a prompt. Accurate context is crucial for LLM applications. If an AI agent doesn't remember that you've changed jobs or confuses the chronology of events, its responses can be jarring or irrelevant, or worse, inaccurate.
                - heading "Zep’s Suboptimal Fact Pipeline" [level=1] [ref=f8e141]
                - paragraph [ref=f8e142]: Before Graphiti, our approach to storing and retrieving user “memory” was, in effect, a specialized RAG pipeline. An LLM extracted “facts” from a user’s chat history. Semantic search, reranking, and other techniques then surfaced facts relevant to the current conversation back to a developer for inclusion in their prompt.
                - paragraph [ref=f8e143]: Unfortunately, this approach became problematic. Reconciling facts from increasingly complex conversations challenged even frontier LLMs such as gpt-4o. We saw incomplete facts, poor recall, and hallucinations. Our RAG search also failed at times to capture the nuanced relationships between facts, leading to irrelevant or contradictory information being retrieved.
                - paragraph [ref=f8e144]: We tried fixing these issues with prompt optimization but saw diminishing returns on effort. We realized that a graph would help model a user’s complex world, potentially addressing these challenges.
                - heading "Building Graphiti" [level=1] [ref=f8e145]
                - paragraph [ref=f8e146]: "We were intrigued by Microsoft’s GraphRAG, which expanded on RAG text chunking with a graph to better model a document corpus. However, it didn't solve our core problem: GraphRAG is designed for static documents and doesn't natively handle temporality."
                - paragraph [ref=f8e147]:
                  - img "uploaded image" [ref=f8e148]
                - paragraph [ref=f8e149]:
                  - text: So, we built Graphiti, a
                  - link "temporal Knowledge Graph" [ref=f8e150]:
                    - /url: https://github.com/getzep/graphiti
                  - text: "library, which is designed from the ground up to handle constantly changing information, hybrid semantic and graph search, and scale:"
                - list [ref=f8e151]:
                  - listitem [ref=f8e152]:
                    - strong [ref=f8e153]: Temporal Awareness
                    - text: ": Tracks changes in facts and relationships over time. Graph edges include temporal metadata to record relationship lifecycles."
                  - listitem [ref=f8e154]:
                    - strong [ref=f8e155]: Episodic Processing
                    - text: ": Ingests data as discrete episodes, maintaining data provenance and enabling incremental processing."
                  - listitem [ref=f8e156]:
                    - strong [ref=f8e157]: Hybrid Search
                    - text: ": Semantic and BM25 full-text search, with the ability to rerank results by distance from a central node."
                  - listitem [ref=f8e158]:
                    - strong [ref=f8e159]: Scalable
                    - text: ": Designed for large datasets, parallelizing LLM calls for batch processing while preserving event chronology."
                  - listitem [ref=f8e160]:
                    - strong [ref=f8e161]: Varied Sources
                    - text: ": Ingests both unstructured text and structured data."
                - heading "Getting Started" [level=1] [ref=f8e162]
                - paragraph [ref=f8e163]:
                  - text: "Graphiti is open-source and available on GitHub:"
                  - link "https://git.new/graphiti" [ref=f8e164]:
                    - /url: https://git.new/graphiti
                - paragraph [ref=f8e165]:
                  - text: "Quick Start:"
                  - code [ref=f8e166]: "`pip install graphiti-core`"
                - paragraph [ref=f8e167]: "While we developed Graphiti for our needs at Zep, we believe it could be useful for any application dealing with evolving, interconnected data, such as:"
                - list [ref=f8e168]:

        - generic [ref=f7e93]: "Artisan builds AI employees for revenue teams. Our first, Ava, is the leading AI BDR: she finds and researches leads across a database of 400M+ contacts, writes and sends personalized email in your tone of voice, runs dialer call steps, handles every reply, and books meetings on the right rep's calendar. Over 90% of our customers run her fully autonomously. Artisan is a complete GTM ecosystem, not a point tool. One platform consolidates the 5-8 tool stack most teams stitch together at $100K+/year: prospecting data and waterfall enrichment (ZoomInfo, Apollo), list building and signals (Clay), sequencing (Outreach, Salesloft), parallel dialing (Nooks, Orum), website visitor identification, and buyer intent. It runs on top of Salesforce and HubSpot with owner mapping, do-not-contact enforcement, and field-level sync controls. We're built for enterprise. SOC 2 Type II, GDPR and CCPA compliant, SSO/SAML, role-based access, workspace isolation per brand, and a full audit trail on everything Ava does. The common enterprise pattern: sales ops runs Ava centrally for a thousand-plus AEs who never log in. Beyond the BDR job, Ava Inbound qualifies and books website visitors from the same knowledge base, and our AI AE runs live product demos and progresses deals. Prospecting, inbound, and the demo on one platform, one knowledge base, one AI sales team. YC W24. $35M+ raised from investors including Y Combinator and HubSpot Ventures. Thousands of customers including DoorDash, Quora, SumUp, CookUnity and SaaStr. Raise sourced over $700K in ARR in six months with Ava. SumUp runs leads at $52 each. Teams in San Francisco and New York. And we're hiring."

              - generic [ref=f8e115]: Founder, Zep AI. Engineer turned startup founder (previously KnowledgeTree) and late-stage operator (SparkPost acquired MessageBird), with detours as a Data Science, Marketing, and Corp Dev guy. Still an engineer at heart and have a soft spot for Go.
        - generic [ref=f8e118]:
          - generic [ref=f8e119]: Company Launches
          - generic [ref=f8e120]:

                - generic [ref=f8e123]: "Graphiti by Zep AI : A library for building dynamic Knowledge Graphs"
                - link "See original launch post" [ref=f8e124]:
                  - /url: /launches/Lmc-graphiti-by-zep-ai-a-library-for-building-dynamic-knowledge-graphs
              - generic [ref=f8e128]:
                - paragraph [ref=f8e129]:
                  - text: Hey! We're Paul, Preston, and Daniel from Zep AI. We've just
                  - link "open-sourced Graphiti" [ref=f8e130]:
                    - /url: https://git.new/graphiti
                  - text: ", a Python library for building temporal Knowledge Graphs using LLMs."
                - paragraph [ref=f8e131]:
                  - link "https://youtu.be/sygRBjILDn8" [ref=f8e132]:

                - iframe [ref=f8e134]:

                              - generic [ref=f9e20]:

                                - link "Zep AI" [ref=f9e22] [cursor=pointer]:
                                  - /url: /channel/UCkDeLVHl3iVYpV8ZdmkfQ-A
                              - generic [ref=f9e24]:
                                - button [ref=f9e25] [cursor=pointer]
                                - generic [ref=f9e27]:
                                  - generic: Zep AI
                                  - generic: 1.18K subscribers
                            - generic [ref=f9e28]:
                              - button "Share" [ref=f9e31] [cursor=pointer]
                              - link "Watch on YouTube" [ref=f9e42] [cursor=pointer]:
                                - /url: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sygRBjILDn8
                                - generic [ref=f9e43]: Watch on
                - paragraph [ref=f8e135]:
                  - text: Graphiti helps you create and query graphs that evolve over time. Think of a knowledge graph as a network of interconnected facts, such as
                  - emphasis [ref=f8e136]: “Kendra loves Adidas shoes.”
                  - text: Each fact is a “triplet, represented by two entities, or nodes (
                  - emphasis [ref=f8e137]: ”Kendra,” “Adidas shoes”
                  - text: ), and their relationship, or edge (
                  - emphasis [ref=f8e138]: ”loves”
                  - text: ). Knowledge Graphs have been explored extensively for information retrieval. What makes Graphiti unique is its ability to autonomously build a knowledge graph while handling changing relationships and maintaining historical context.
                - paragraph [ref=f8e139]:
                  - text: At Zep, we build a
                  - link "memory layer for LLM applications" [ref=f8e140]:
                    - /url: https://www.getzep.com
                  - text: . Developers use Zep to recall relevant user information from past conversations without including the entire chat history in a prompt. Accurate context is crucial for LLM applications. If an AI agent doesn't remember that you've changed jobs or confuses the chronology of events, its responses can be jarring or irrelevant, or worse, inaccurate.
                - heading "Zep’s Suboptimal Fact Pipeline" [level=1] [ref=f8e141]
                - paragraph [ref=f8e142]: Before Graphiti, our approach to storing and retrieving user “memory” was, in effect, a specialized RAG pipeline. An LLM extracted “facts” from a user’s chat history. Semantic search, reranking, and other techniques then surfaced facts relevant to the current conversation back to a developer for inclusion in their prompt.
                - paragraph [ref=f8e143]: Unfortunately, this approach became problematic. Reconciling facts from increasingly complex conversations challenged even frontier LLMs such as gpt-4o. We saw incomplete facts, poor recall, and hallucinations. Our RAG search also failed at times to capture the nuanced relationships between facts, leading to irrelevant or contradictory information being retrieved.
                - paragraph [ref=f8e144]: We tried fixing these issues with prompt optimization but saw diminishing returns on effort. We realized that a graph would help model a user’s complex world, potentially addressing these challenges.
                - heading "Building Graphiti" [level=1] [ref=f8e145]
                - paragraph [ref=f8e146]: "We were intrigued by Microsoft’s GraphRAG, which expanded on RAG text chunking with a graph to better model a document corpus. However, it didn't solve our core problem: GraphRAG is designed for static documents and doesn't natively handle temporality."
                - paragraph [ref=f8e147]:
                  - img "uploaded image" [ref=f8e148]
                - paragraph [ref=f8e149]:
                  - text: So, we built Graphiti, a
                  - link "temporal Knowledge Graph" [ref=f8e150]:
                    - /url: https://github.com/getzep/graphiti
                  - text: "library, which is designed from the ground up to handle constantly changing information, hybrid semantic and graph search, and scale:"
                - list [ref=f8e151]:
                  - listitem [ref=f8e152]:
                    - strong [ref=f8e153]: Temporal Awareness
                    - text: ": Tracks changes in facts and relationships over time. Graph edges include temporal metadata to record relationship lifecycles."
                  - listitem [ref=f8e154]:
                    - strong [ref=f8e155]: Episodic Processing
                    - text: ": Ingests data as discrete episodes, maintaining data provenance and enabling incremental processing."
                  - listitem [ref=f8e156]:
                    - strong [ref=f8e157]: Hybrid Search
                    - text: ": Semantic and BM25 full-text search, with the ability to rerank results by distance from a central node."
                  - listitem [ref=f8e158]:
                    - strong [ref=f8e159]: Scalable
                    - text: ": Designed for large datasets, parallelizing LLM calls for batch processing while preserving event chronology."
                  - listitem [ref=f8e160]:
                    - strong [ref=f8e161]: Varied Sources
                    - text: ": Ingests both unstructured text and structured data."
                - heading "Getting Started" [level=1] [ref=f8e162]
                - paragraph [ref=f8e163]:
                  - text: "Graphiti is open-source and available on GitHub:"
                  - link "https://git.new/graphiti" [ref=f8e164]:
                    - /url: https://git.new/graphiti
                - paragraph [ref=f8e165]:
                  - text: "Quick Start:"
                  - code [ref=f8e166]: "`pip install graphiti-core`"
                - paragraph [ref=f8e167]: "While we developed Graphiti for our needs at Zep, we believe it could be useful for any application dealing with evolving, interconnected data, such as:"
                - list [ref=f8e168]:
                  - listitem [ref=f8e169]: Personal AI assistants that need to maintain user context over time
                  - listitem [ref=f8e170]: Knowledge management systems for rapidly changing domains
                  - listitem [ref=f8e171]: Social network analysis tools
                  - listitem [ref=f8e172]: Financial systems tracking changing relationships and transactions
                - paragraph [ref=f8e173]: If you try, we'd love to hear your thoughts, questions, and experiences. Please also consider contributing!

        - generic [ref=f7e93]: "Artisan builds AI employees for revenue teams. Our first, Ava, is the leading AI BDR: she finds and researches leads across a database of 400M+ contacts, writes and sends personalized email in your tone of voice, runs dialer call steps, handles every reply, and books meetings on the right rep's calendar. Over 90% of our customers run her fully autonomously. Artisan is a complete GTM ecosystem, not a point tool. One platform consolidates the 5-8 tool stack most teams stitch together at $100K+/year: prospecting data and waterfall enrichment (ZoomInfo, Apollo), list building and signals (Clay), sequencing (Outreach, Salesloft), parallel dialing (Nooks, Orum), website visitor identification, and buyer intent. It runs on top of Salesforce and HubSpot with owner mapping, do-not-contact enforcement, and field-level sync controls. We're built for enterprise. SOC 2 Type II, GDPR and CCPA compliant, SSO/SAML, role-based access, workspace isolation per brand, and a full audit trail on everything Ava does. The common enterprise pattern: sales ops runs Ava centrally for a thousand-plus AEs who never log in. Beyond the BDR job, Ava Inbound qualifies and books website visitors from the same knowledge base, and our AI AE runs live product demos and progresses deals. Prospecting, inbound, and the demo on one platform, one knowledge base, one AI sales team. YC W24. $35M+ raised from investors including Y Combinator and HubSpot Ventures. Thousands of customers including DoorDash, Quora, SumUp, CookUnity and SaaStr. Raise sourced over $700K in ARR in six months with Ava. SumUp runs leads at $52 each. Teams in San Francisco and New York. And we're hiring."

              - generic [ref=f8e115]: Founder, Zep AI. Engineer turned startup founder (previously KnowledgeTree) and late-stage operator (SparkPost acquired MessageBird), with detours as a Data Science, Marketing, and Corp Dev guy. Still an engineer at heart and have a soft spot for Go.
        - generic [ref=f8e118]:
          - generic [ref=f8e119]: Company Launches
          - generic [ref=f8e120]:
            - generic [ref=f8e121] [cursor=pointer]:
              - generic [ref=f8e122]:
                - generic [ref=f8e123]: "Graphiti by Zep AI : A library for building dynamic Knowledge Graphs"
                - link "See original launch post" [ref=f8e124]:
                  - /url: /launches/Lmc-graphiti-by-zep-ai-a-library-for-building-dynamic-knowledge-graphs
              - generic [ref=f8e128]:
                - paragraph [ref=f8e129]:
                  - text: Hey! We're Paul, Preston, and Daniel from Zep AI. We've just
                  - link "open-sourced Graphiti" [ref=f8e130]:
                    - /url: https://git.new/graphiti
                  - text: ", a Python library for building temporal Knowledge Graphs using LLMs."
                - paragraph [ref=f8e131]:
                  - link "https://youtu.be/sygRBjILDn8" [ref=f8e132]:
                    - /url: https://youtu.be/sygRBjILDn8
                - iframe [ref=f8e134]:

                    - generic [ref=f9e5]:
                      - generic:

                          - button "Hide player controls" [ref=f9e12] [cursor=pointer]
                          - generic [ref=f9e14]:
                            - generic [ref=f9e19]:
                              - generic [ref=f9e20]:
                                - link "Graphiti - Temporal Knowledge Graphs for AI Agents" [ref=f9e21] [cursor=pointer]:
                                  - /url: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sygRBjILDn8
                                - link "Zep AI" [ref=f9e22] [cursor=pointer]:
                                  - /url: /channel/UCkDeLVHl3iVYpV8ZdmkfQ-A
                              - generic [ref=f9e24]:
                                - button [ref=f9e25] [cursor=pointer]
                                - generic [ref=f9e27]:
                                  - generic: Zep AI
                                  - generic: 1.18K subscribers
                            - generic [ref=f9e28]:
                              - button "Share" [ref=f9e31] [cursor=pointer]
                              - link "Watch on YouTube" [ref=f9e42] [cursor=pointer]:
                                - /url: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sygRBjILDn8
                                - generic [ref=f9e43]: Watch on
                - paragraph [ref=f8e135]:
                  - text: Graphiti helps you create and query graphs that evolve over time. Think of a knowledge graph as a network of interconnected facts, such as
                  - emphasis [ref=f8e136]: “Kendra loves Adidas shoes.”
                  - text: Each fact is a “triplet, represented by two entities, or nodes (
                  - emphasis [ref=f8e137]: ”Kendra,” “Adidas shoes”
                  - text: ), and their relationship, or edge (
                  - emphasis [ref=f8e138]: ”loves”
                  - text: ). Knowledge Graphs have been explored extensively for information retrieval. What makes Graphiti unique is its ability to autonomously build a knowledge graph while handling changing relationships and maintaining historical context.
                - paragraph [ref=f8e139]:
                  - text: At Zep, we build a
                  - link "memory layer for LLM applications" [ref=f8e140]:
                    - /url: https://www.getzep.com
                  - text: . Developers use Zep to recall relevant user information from past conversations without including the entire chat history in a prompt. Accurate context is crucial for LLM applications. If an AI agent doesn't remember that you've changed jobs or confuses the chronology of events, its responses can be jarring or irrelevant, or worse, inaccurate.
                - heading "Zep’s Suboptimal Fact Pipeline" [level=1] [ref=f8e141]
                - paragraph [ref=f8e142]: Before Graphiti, our approach to storing and retrieving user “memory” was, in effect, a specialized RAG pipeline. An LLM extracted “facts” from a user’s chat history. Semantic search, reranking, and other techniques then surfaced facts relevant to the current conversation back to a developer for inclusion in their prompt.
                - paragraph [ref=f8e143]: Unfortunately, this approach became problematic. Reconciling facts from increasingly complex conversations challenged even frontier LLMs such as gpt-4o. We saw incomplete facts, poor recall, and hallucinations. Our RAG search also failed at times to capture the nuanced relationships between facts, leading to irrelevant or contradictory information being retrieved.
                - paragraph [ref=f8e144]: We tried fixing these issues with prompt optimization but saw diminishing returns on effort. We realized that a graph would help model a user’s complex world, potentially addressing these challenges.
                - heading "Building Graphiti" [level=1] [ref=f8e145]
                - paragraph [ref=f8e146]: "We were intrigued by Microsoft’s GraphRAG, which expanded on RAG text chunking with a graph to better model a document corpus. However, it didn't solve our core problem: GraphRAG is designed for static documents and doesn't natively handle temporality."
                - paragraph [ref=f8e147]:
                  - img "uploaded image" [ref=f8e148]
                - paragraph [ref=f8e149]:
                  - text: So, we built Graphiti, a
                  - link "temporal Knowledge Graph" [ref=f8e150]:
                    - /url: https://github.com/getzep/graphiti
                  - text: "library, which is designed from the ground up to handle constantly changing information, hybrid semantic and graph search, and scale:"
                - list [ref=f8e151]:
                  - listitem [ref=f8e152]:
                    - strong [ref=f8e153]: Temporal Awareness
                    - text: ": Tracks changes in facts and relationships over time. Graph edges include temporal metadata to record relationship lifecycles."
                  - listitem [ref=f8e154]:
                    - strong [ref=f8e155]: Episodic Processing
                    - text: ": Ingests data as discrete episodes, maintaining data provenance and enabling incremental processing."
                  - listitem [ref=f8e156]:
                    - strong [ref=f8e157]: Hybrid Search
                    - text: ": Semantic and BM25 full-text search, with the ability to rerank results by distance from a central node."
                  - listitem [ref=f8e158]:
                    - strong [ref=f8e159]: Scalable
                    - text: ": Designed for large datasets, parallelizing LLM calls for batch processing while preserving event chronology."
                  - listitem [ref=f8e160]:
                    - strong [ref=f8e161]: Varied Sources
                    - text: ": Ingests both unstructured text and structured data."
                - heading "Getting Started" [level=1] [ref=f8e162]
                - paragraph [ref=f8e163]:
                  - text: "Graphiti is open-source and available on GitHub:"
                  - link "https://git.new/graphiti" [ref=f8e164]:
                    - /url: https://git.new/graphiti
                - paragraph [ref=f8e165]:
                  - text: "Quick Start:"

        - generic [ref=f7e93]: "Artisan builds AI employees for revenue teams. Our first, Ava, is the leading AI BDR: she finds and researches leads across a database of 400M+ contacts, writes and sends personalized email in your tone of voice, runs dialer call steps, handles every reply, and books meetings on the right rep's calendar. Over 90% of our customers run her fully autonomously. Artisan is a complete GTM ecosystem, not a point tool. One platform consolidates the 5-8 tool stack most teams stitch together at $100K+/year: prospecting data and waterfall enrichment (ZoomInfo, Apollo), list building and signals (Clay), sequencing (Outreach, Salesloft), parallel dialing (Nooks, Orum), website visitor identification, and buyer intent. It runs on top of Salesforce and HubSpot with owner mapping, do-not-contact enforcement, and field-level sync controls. We're built for enterprise. SOC 2 Type II, GDPR and CCPA compliant, SSO/SAML, role-based access, workspace isolation per brand, and a full audit trail on everything Ava does. The common enterprise pattern: sales ops runs Ava centrally for a thousand-plus AEs who never log in. Beyond the BDR job, Ava Inbound qualifies and books website visitors from the same knowledge base, and our AI AE runs live product demos and progresses deals. Prospecting, inbound, and the demo on one platform, one knowledge base, one AI sales team. YC W24. $35M+ raised from investors including Y Combinator and HubSpot Ventures. Thousands of customers including DoorDash, Quora, SumUp, CookUnity and SaaStr. Raise sourced over $700K in ARR in six months with Ava. SumUp runs leads at $52 each. Teams in San Francisco and New York. And we're hiring."

              - generic [ref=f8e115]: Founder, Zep AI. Engineer turned startup founder (previously KnowledgeTree) and late-stage operator (SparkPost acquired MessageBird), with detours as a Data Science, Marketing, and Corp Dev guy. Still an engineer at heart and have a soft spot for Go.

                - link "See original launch post" [ref=f8e124]:

              - generic [ref=f8e128]:
                - paragraph [ref=f8e129]:
                  - text: Hey! We're Paul, Preston, and Daniel from Zep AI. We've just
                  - link "open-sourced Graphiti" [ref=f8e130]:

                  - text: ", a Python library for building temporal Knowledge Graphs using LLMs."

                                - link "Zep AI" [ref=f9e22] [cursor=pointer]:

                                - generic [ref=f9e43]: Watch on
                - paragraph [ref=f8e135]:
                  - text: Graphiti helps you create and query graphs that evolve over time. Think of a knowledge graph as a network of interconnected facts, such as
                  - emphasis [ref=f8e136]: “Kendra loves Adidas shoes.”
                  - text: Each fact is a “triplet, represented by two entities, or nodes (
                  - emphasis [ref=f8e137]: ”Kendra,” “Adidas shoes”
                  - text: ), and their relationship, or edge (
                  - emphasis [ref=f8e138]: ”loves”
                  - text: ). Knowledge Graphs have been explored extensively for information retrieval. What makes Graphiti unique is its ability to autonomously build a knowledge graph while handling changing relationships and maintaining historical context.
                - paragraph [ref=f8e139]:
                  - text: At Zep, we build a
                  - link "memory layer for LLM applications" [ref=f8e140]:
                    - /url: https://www.getzep.com
                  - text: . Developers use Zep to recall relevant user information from past conversations without including the entire chat history in a prompt. Accurate context is crucial for LLM applications. If an AI agent doesn't remember that you've changed jobs or confuses the chronology of events, its responses can be jarring or irrelevant, or worse, inaccurate.
                - heading "Zep’s Suboptimal Fact Pipeline" [level=1] [ref=f8e141]
                - paragraph [ref=f8e142]: Before Graphiti, our approach to storing and retrieving user “memory” was, in effect, a specialized RAG pipeline. An LLM extracted “facts” from a user’s chat history. Semantic search, reranking, and other techniques then surfaced facts relevant to the current conversation back to a developer for inclusion in their prompt.
                - paragraph [ref=f8e143]: Unfortunately, this approach became problematic. Reconciling facts from increasingly complex conversations challenged even frontier LLMs such as gpt-4o. We saw incomplete facts, poor recall, and hallucinations. Our RAG search also failed at times to capture the nuanced relationships between facts, leading to irrelevant or contradictory information being retrieved.
                - paragraph [ref=f8e144]: We tried fixing these issues with prompt optimization but saw diminishing returns on effort. We realized that a graph would help model a user’s complex world, potentially addressing these challenges.
                - heading "Building Graphiti" [level=1] [ref=f8e145]
                - paragraph [ref=f8e146]: "We were intrigued by Microsoft’s GraphRAG, which expanded on RAG text chunking with a graph to better model a document corpus. However, it didn't solve our core problem: GraphRAG is designed for static documents and doesn't natively handle temporality."
                - paragraph [ref=f8e147]:
                  - img "uploaded image" [ref=f8e148]
                - paragraph [ref=f8e149]:
                  - text: So, we built Graphiti, a
                  - link "temporal Knowledge Graph" [ref=f8e150]:
                    - /url: https://github.com/getzep/graphiti
                  - text: "library, which is designed from the ground up to handle constantly changing information, hybrid semantic and graph search, and scale:"
                - list [ref=f8e151]:
                  - listitem [ref=f8e152]:
                    - strong [ref=f8e153]: Temporal Awareness
                    - text: ": Tracks changes in facts and relationships over time. Graph edges include temporal metadata to record relationship lifecycles."
                  - listitem [ref=f8e154]:
                    - strong [ref=f8e155]: Episodic Processing
                    - text: ": Ingests data as discrete episodes, maintaining data provenance and enabling incremental processing."
                  - listitem [ref=f8e156]:
                    - strong [ref=f8e157]: Hybrid Search
                    - text: ": Semantic and BM25 full-text search, with the ability to rerank results by distance from a central node."
                  - listitem [ref=f8e158]:
                    - strong [ref=f8e159]: Scalable
                    - text: ": Designed for large datasets, parallelizing LLM calls for batch processing while preserving event chronology."
                  - listitem [ref=f8e160]:
                    - strong [ref=f8e161]: Varied Sources
                    - text: ": Ingests both unstructured text and structured data."
                - heading "Getting Started" [level=1] [ref=f8e162]
                - paragraph [ref=f8e163]:
                  - text: "Graphiti is open-source and available on GitHub:"
                  - link "https://git.new/graphiti" [ref=f8e164]:
                    - /url: https://git.new/graphiti
                - paragraph [ref=f8e165]:
                  - text: "Quick Start:"
                  - code [ref=f8e166]: "`pip install graphiti-core`"
                - paragraph [ref=f8e167]: "While we developed Graphiti for our needs at Zep, we believe it could be useful for any application dealing with evolving, interconnected data, such as:"
                - list [ref=f8e168]:
                  - listitem [ref=f8e169]: Personal AI assistants that need to maintain user context over time
                  - listitem [ref=f8e170]: Knowledge management systems for rapidly changing domains
                  - listitem [ref=f8e171]: Social network analysis tools
                  - listitem [ref=f8e172]: Financial systems tracking changing relationships and transactions
                - paragraph [ref=f8e173]: If you try, we'd love to hear your thoughts, questions, and experiences. Please also consider contributing!

        - generic [ref=f7e93]: "Artisan builds AI employees for revenue teams. Our first, Ava, is the leading AI BDR: she finds and researches leads across a database of 400M+ contacts, writes and sends personalized email in your tone of voice, runs dialer call steps, handles every reply, and books meetings on the right rep's calendar. Over 90% of our customers run her fully autonomously. Artisan is a complete GTM ecosystem, not a point tool. One platform consolidates the 5-8 tool stack most teams stitch together at $100K+/year: prospecting data and waterfall enrichment (ZoomInfo, Apollo), list building and signals (Clay), sequencing (Outreach, Salesloft), parallel dialing (Nooks, Orum), website visitor identification, and buyer intent. It runs on top of Salesforce and HubSpot with owner mapping, do-not-contact enforcement, and field-level sync controls. We're built for enterprise. SOC 2 Type II, GDPR and CCPA compliant, SSO/SAML, role-based access, workspace isolation per brand, and a full audit trail on everything Ava does. The common enterprise pattern: sales ops runs Ava centrally for a thousand-plus AEs who never log in. Beyond the BDR job, Ava Inbound qualifies and books website visitors from the same knowledge base, and our AI AE runs live product demos and progresses deals. Prospecting, inbound, and the demo on one platform, one knowledge base, one AI sales team. YC W24. $35M+ raised from investors including Y Combinator and HubSpot Ventures.                 - paragraph [ref=f8e135]:
                  - text: Graphiti helps you create and query graphs that evolve over time. Think of a knowledge graph as a network of interconnected facts, such as
                  - emphasis [ref=f8e136]: “Kendra loves Adidas shoes.”
                  - text: Each fact is a “triplet, represented by two entities, or nodes (
                  - emphasis [ref=f8e137]: ”Kendra,” “Adidas shoes”
                  - text: ), and their relationship, or edge (
                  - emphasis [ref=f8e138]: ”loves”
                  - text: ). Knowledge Graphs have been explored extensively for information retrieval. What makes Graphiti unique is its ability to autonomously build a knowledge graph while handling changing relationships and maintaining historical context.
                - paragraph [ref=f8e139]:
                  - text: At Zep, we build a
                  - link "memory layer for LLM applications" [ref=f8e140]:
                    - /url: https://www.getzep.com
                  - text: . Developers use Zep to recall relevant user information from past conversations without including the entire chat history in a prompt. Accurate context is crucial for LLM applications. If an AI agent doesn't remember that you've changed jobs or confuses the chronology of events, its responses can be jarring or irrelevant, or worse, inaccurate.
                - heading "Zep’s Suboptimal Fact Pipeline" [level=1] [ref=f8e141]
                - paragraph [ref=f8e142]: Before Graphiti, our approach to storing and retrieving user “memory” was, in effect, a specialized RAG pipeline. An LLM extracted “facts” from a user’s chat history. Semantic search, reranking, and other techniques then surfaced facts relevant to the current conversation back to a developer for inclusion in their prompt.
                - paragraph [ref=f8e143]: Unfortunately, this approach became problematic. Reconciling facts from increasingly complex conversations challenged even frontier LLMs such as gpt-4o. We saw incomplete facts, poor recall, and hallucinations. Our RAG search also failed at times to capture the nuanced relationships between facts, leading to irrelevant or contradictory information being retrieved.
                - paragraph [ref=f8e144]: We tried fixing these issues with prompt optimization but saw diminishing returns on effort. We realized that a graph would help model a user’s complex world, potentially addressing these challenges.
                - heading "Building Graphiti" [level=1] [ref=f8e145]
                - paragraph [ref=f8e146]: "We were intrigued by Microsoft’s GraphRAG, which expanded on RAG text chunking with a graph to better model a document corpus. However, it didn't solve our core problem: GraphRAG is designed for static documents and doesn't natively handle temporality."
                - paragraph [ref=f8e147]:
                  - img "uploaded image" [ref=f8e148]
                - paragraph [ref=f8e149]:
                  - text: So, we built Graphiti, a
                  - link "temporal Knowledge Graph" [ref=f8e150]:
                    - /url: https://github.com/getzep/graphiti
                  - text: "library, which is designed from the ground up to handle constantly changing information, hybrid semantic and graph search, and scale:"
                - list [ref=f8e151]:
                  - listitem [ref=f8e152]:
                    - strong [ref=f8e153]: Temporal Awareness
                    - text: ": Tracks changes in facts and relationships over time. Graph edges include temporal metadata to record relationship lifecycles."
                  - listitem [ref=f8e154]:
                    - strong [ref=f8e155]: Episodic Processing
                    - text: ": Ingests data as discrete episodes, maintaining data provenance and enabling incremental processing."
                  - listitem [ref=f8e156]:
                    - strong [ref=f8e157]: Hybrid Search
                    - text: ": Semantic and BM25 full-text search, with the ability to rerank results by distance from a central node."
                  - listitem [ref=f8e158]:
                    - strong [ref=f8e159]: Scalable
                    - text: ": Designed for large datasets, parallelizing LLM calls for batch processing while preserving event chronology."
                  - listitem [ref=f8e160]:
                    - strong [ref=f8e161]: Varied Sources
                    - text: ": Ingests both unstructured text and structured data."
                - heading "Getting Started" [level=1] [ref=f8e162]
                - paragraph [ref=f8e163]:
                  - text: "Graphiti is open-source and available on GitHub:"
                  - link "https://git.new/graphiti" [ref=f8e164]:
                    - /url: https://git.new/graphiti
                - paragraph [ref=f8e165]:
                  - text: "Quick Start:"
                  - code [ref=f8e166]: "`pip install graphiti-core`"
                - paragraph [ref=f8e167]: "While we developed Graphiti for our needs at Zep, we believe it could be useful for any application dealing with evolving, interconnected data, such as:"
                - list [ref=f8e168]:
                  - listitem [ref=f8e169]: Personal AI assistants that need to maintain user context over time
                  - listitem [ref=f8e170]: Knowledge management systems for rapidly changing domains
                  - listitem [ref=f8e171]: Social network analysis tools
                  - listitem [ref=f8e172]: Financial systems tracking changing relationships and transactions
                - paragraph [ref=f8e173]: If you try, we'd love to hear your thoughts, questions, and experiences. Please also consider contributing!
                - paragraph [ref=f8e174]:
                  - img "uploaded image" [ref=f8e175]

Bing Wu,https://linkedin.com/in/binw,"Subject: Quick question about Retell AI's voice agent stack

Hi Bing,

I've been following Retell AI since your TechCrunch feature and I'm impressed by the sub-second response times you've achieved for human-like voice agents — going from ByteDance/TikTok product work to building infrastructure other AI voice teams rely on is a great arc.

I work with companies building on top of conversational AI infrastructure and think there could be a valuable connection between what we're doing and where Retell AI is headed with contact center automation.

Would you be open to a 15-minute call in the next week or two? I'd love to learn more about your roadmap and see if there's a fit.

Best,
[Your Name]"
Todd Li,https://www.linkedin.com/in/toddli1/,"Subject: 15 minutes re: Retell AI's growth as President

Hi Todd,

Congrats on Retell AI's traction — building an API that lets any developer create human-like voice agents is exactly the kind of infrastructure the AI voice space needs right now. Your role steering the business side alongside Bing's product vision stood out to me.

I'd love to share a bit about what we're working on and hear how you're thinking about scaling contact center partnerships this year.

Could we grab 15 minutes on a call sometime this week or next?

Best,
[Your Name]"
Evie Wang,https://linkedin.com/in/yanwang131415,"Subject: Loved Retell AI's design-led approach — 15 min call?

Hi Evie,

Your background as a product designer at ByteDance clearly shows in Retell AI's polish — the demo experience is one of the cleanest I've seen in the voice AI space. As CMO, I imagine you're also thinking hard about how to position Retell AI as the category matures.

I'd love to connect briefly to share what we're building and explore whether there's a way to collaborate or support your growth story.

Do you have 15 minutes for a quick call this week?

Best,
[Your Name]"
Weijia Yu,https://linkedin.com/in/weijia-y-76b816194,"Subject: Question about Retell AI's ML/speech stack

Hi Weijia,

Your path from Meta to ObEN to Retell AI is a great fit for the hard problems you're solving in real-time speech and TTS pipelines. I'm reaching out because I think there's a relevant overlap with what we're building on the applied ML side.

Would you be open to a 15-minute call to trade notes on the technical challenges of low-latency voice agents and see if there's a way we could help each other?

Best,
[Your Name]"
Zexia Zhang,https://linkedin.com/in/zexia-zhang-171480133,"Subject: Retell AI's speech tech — quick 15-min chat?

Hi Zexia,

Four years leading speech translation and NLP for call analysis at Google is exactly the kind of deep expertise that makes Retell AI's low-latency voice agents possible. I'd love to learn more about the architecture decisions behind your 800ms response times.

I think there could be a good reason for us to connect given the work we're doing in adjacent AI infrastructure.

Would you have 15 minutes for a call in the next week or so?

Best,
[Your Name]"
Daksh Gupta,https://linkedin.com/in/dakshg,"Subject: Greptile's approach to codebase-aware AI — 15 min?

Hi Daksh,

Congrats on Greptile's Series A and the v3 launch — the idea of giving LLMs full context of a codebase to catch more bugs and speed up PR reviews is a problem every engineering team feels. I liked your line about the Amazon locker, by the way.

I'm reaching out because I think there's a natural connection between what we're working on and Greptile's mission to make AI code review genuinely useful at scale.

Could we set up a quick 15-minute call to explore this?

Best,
[Your Name]"
Soohoon Choi,https://linkedin.com/in/soohoonchoi,"Subject: Quick 15 min re: Greptile's CTO roadmap

Hi Soohoon,

As CTO of Greptile, you're tackling one of the trickiest problems in applied AI — indexing and reasoning over huge, messy codebases so LLMs can actually help. That's a hard technical bar, and it shows in the results you're getting for teams like PostHog and Raycast.

I'd love to share what we're building and hear more about the technical direction of Greptile's context engine.

Would you be free for a 15-minute call sometime this week?

Best,
[Your Name]"
Vaishant Kameswaran,https://linkedin.com/in/vaishant,"Subject: Greptile + a quick 15-minute intro call

Hi Vaishant,

Your CS and linguistics background at Georgia Tech seems like a great combination for the natural-language-meets-code problem Greptile is solving. Millions of PR changes reviewed weekly is a serious scale milestone.

I think there's a good reason for us to connect given the space we're both operating in — would you be open to a short 15-minute call to compare notes?

Best,
[Your Name]"
Jaspar Carmichael-Jack,https://linkedin.com/in/jaspar-carmichael-jack,"Subject: Artisan's AI BDR Ava — 15-minute call?

Hi Jaspar,

Artisan's growth from a $2.3M pre-seed to a $35M+ raised, thousand-plus-AE enterprise deployment story is genuinely impressive — Ava sounds like one of the most complete 'AI employee' products out there for outbound sales.

I'd love to learn more about how you're scaling Artisan's GTM platform and share a bit about what we're building that could be relevant to your roadmap.

Do you have 15 minutes for a call in the next week or two?

Best,
[Your Name]"
Daniel Chalef,https://linkedin.com/in/danielchalef,"Subject: Zep AI's Graphiti and temporal memory — 15 min?

Hi Daniel,

Graphiti hitting 20k GitHub stars in under a year says a lot about how badly the market needed a real solution for temporal knowledge graphs and agent memory. Your path from KnowledgeTree through the SparkPost/MessageBird world into Zep AI is a great founder story.

I'm reaching out because I think there's a strong connection between what we're building and Zep's memory layer for LLM applications.

Would you be open to a quick 15-minute call to explore this further?

Best,
[Your Name]"
Michael Rosenfield,https://linkedin.com/in/rosenfieldmichael,"Subject: Decipher AI's QA agents — quick 15-min call?

Hi Michael,

Going from leading Google Maps ad formats and Pixel's premium product line to building QA agents that write and maintain E2E tests 10x faster is a compelling pivot — especially now that coding agents are shipping code faster than traditional QA can keep up.

I'd love to hear more about how Decipher AI is thinking about the agentic QA space and share what we're working on.

Could we find 15 minutes for a call this week or next?

Best,
[Your Name]"
Rohan Das,https://linkedin.com/in/rohan-d,"Subject: Decipher AI's vision-based bug detection — 15 min?

Hi Rohan,

Rebuilding the YouTube homepage service to handle billions of daily requests is serious infrastructure experience, and it clearly informs how Decipher AI approaches reliability — using vision AI to catch bugs in live user sessions is a smart, practical approach to QA.

I think there's a good fit between what we're building and Decipher's mission to keep QA in step with AI-accelerated shipping.

Would you have 15 minutes for a call sometime soon?

Best,
[Your Name]"

        - generic [ref=f7e93]: "Artisan builds AI employees for revenue teams. Our first, Ava, is the leading AI BDR: she finds and researches leads across a database of 400M+ contacts, writes and sends personalized email in your tone of voice, runs dialer call steps, handles every reply, and books meetings on the right rep's calendar. Over 90% of our customers run her fully autonomously. Artisan is a complete GTM ecosystem, not a point tool. One platform consolidates the 5-8 tool stack most teams stitch together at $100K+/year: prospecting data and waterfall enrichment (ZoomInfo, Apollo), list building and signals (Clay), sequencing (Outreach, Salesloft), parallel dialing (Nooks, Orum), website visitor identification, and buyer intent. It runs on top of Salesforce and HubSpot with owner mapping, do-not-contact enforcement, and field-level sync controls. We're built for enterprise. SOC 2 Type II, GDPR and CCPA compliant, SSO/SAML, role-based access, workspace isolation per brand, and a full audit trail on everything Ava does. The common enterprise pattern: sales ops runs Ava centrally for a thousand-plus AEs who never log in. Beyond the BDR job, Ava Inbound qualifies and books website visitors from the same knowledge base, and our AI AE runs live product demos and progresses deals. Prospecting, inbound, and the demo on one platform, one knowledge base, one AI sales team. YC W24. $35M+ raised from investors including Y Combinator and HubSpot Ventures. Thousands of customers including DoorDash, Quora, SumUp, CookUnity and SaaStr. Raise sourced over $700K in ARR in six months with Ava. SumUp runs leads at $52 each. Teams in San Francisco and New York. And we're hiring."

              - generic [ref=f8e115]: Founder, Zep AI. Engineer turned startup founder (previously KnowledgeTree) and late-stage operator (SparkPost acquired MessageBird), with detours as a Data Science, Marketing, and Corp Dev guy. Still an engineer at heart and have a soft spot for Go.

          - generic [ref=f8e119]: Company Launches

                - generic [ref=f8e123]: "Graphiti by Zep AI : A library for building dynamic Knowledge Graphs"
                - link "See original launch post" [ref=f8e124]:
                  - /url: /launches/Lmc-graphiti-by-zep-ai-a-library-for-building-dynamic-knowledge-graphs
              - generic [ref=f8e128]:
                - paragraph [ref=f8e129]:
                  - text: Hey! We're Paul, Preston, and Daniel from Zep AI. We've just
                  - link "open-sourced Graphiti" [ref=f8e130]:
                    - /url: https://git.new/graphiti
                  - text: ", a Python library for building temporal Knowledge Graphs using LLMs."
                - paragraph [ref=f8e131]:

                                - link "Zep AI" [ref=f9e22] [cursor=pointer]:
                                  - /url: /channel/UCkDeLVHl3iVYpV8ZdmkfQ-A
                              - generic [ref=f9e24]:
                                - button [ref=f9e25] [cursor=pointer]

                                  - generic: Zep AI
                                  - generic: 1.18K subscribers
                            - generic [ref=f9e28]:

                                - /url: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sygRBjILDn8
                                - generic [ref=f9e43]: Watch on
                - paragraph [ref=f8e135]:
                  - text: Graphiti helps you create and query graphs that evolve over time. Think of a knowledge graph as a network of interconnected facts, such as
                  - emphasis [ref=f8e136]: “Kendra loves Adidas shoes.”
                  - text: Each fact is a “triplet, represented by two entities, or nodes (
                  - emphasis [ref=f8e137]: ”Kendra,” “Adidas shoes”
                  - text: ), and their relationship, or edge (
                  - emphasis [ref=f8e138]: ”loves”
                  - text: ). Knowledge Graphs have been explored extensively for information retrieval. What makes Graphiti unique is its ability to autonomously build a knowledge graph while handling changing relationships and maintaining historical context.
                - paragraph [ref=f8e139]:
                  - text: At Zep, we build a
                  - link "memory layer for LLM applications" [ref=f8e140]:
                    - /url: https://www.getzep.com
                  - text: . Developers use Zep to recall relevant user information from past conversations without including the entire chat history in a prompt. Accurate context is crucial for LLM applications. If an AI agent doesn't remember that you've changed jobs or confuses the chronology of events, its responses can be jarring or irrelevant, or worse, inaccurate.
                - heading "Zep’s Suboptimal Fact Pipeline" [level=1] [ref=f8e141]
                - paragraph [ref=f8e142]: Before Graphiti, our approach to storing and retrieving user “memory” was, in effect, a specialized RAG pipeline. An LLM extracted “facts” from a user’s chat history. Semantic search, reranking, and other techniques then surfaced facts relevant to the current conversation back to a developer for inclusion in their prompt.
                - paragraph [ref=f8e143]: Unfortunately, this approach became problematic. Reconciling facts from increasingly complex conversations challenged even frontier LLMs such as gpt-4o. We saw incomplete facts, poor recall, and hallucinations. Our RAG search also failed at times to capture the nuanced relationships between facts, leading to irrelevant or contradictory information being retrieved.
                - paragraph [ref=f8e144]: We tried fixing these issues with prompt optimization but saw diminishing returns on effort. We realized that a graph would help model a user’s complex world, potentially addressing these challenges.
                - heading "Building Graphiti" [level=1] [ref=f8e145]
                - paragraph [ref=f8e146]: "We were intrigued by Microsoft’s GraphRAG, which expanded on RAG text chunking with a graph to better model a document corpus. However, it didn't solve our core problem: GraphRAG is designed for static documents and doesn't natively handle temporality."
                - paragraph [ref=f8e147]:
                  - img "uploaded image" [ref=f8e148]
                - paragraph [ref=f8e149]:
                  - text: So, we built Graphiti, a
                  - link "temporal Knowledge Graph" [ref=f8e150]:
                    - /url: https://github.com/getzep/graphiti
                  - text: "library, which is designed from the ground up to handle constantly changing information, hybrid semantic and graph search, and scale:"
                - list [ref=f8e151]:
                  - listitem [ref=f8e152]:
                    - strong [ref=f8e153]: Temporal Awareness
                    - text: ": Tracks changes in facts and relationships over time. Graph edges include temporal metadata to record relationship lifecycles."
                  - listitem [ref=f8e154]:
                    - strong [ref=f8e155]: Episodic Processing
                    - text: ": Ingests data as discrete episodes, maintaining data provenance and enabling incremental processing."
                  - listitem [ref=f8e156]:
                    - strong [ref=f8e157]: Hybrid Search
                    - text: ": Semantic and BM25 full-text search, with the ability to rerank results by distance from a central node."
                  - listitem [ref=f8e158]:
                    - strong [ref=f8e159]: Scalable
                    - text: ": Designed for large datasets, parallelizing LLM calls for batch processing while preserving event chronology."
                  - listitem [ref=f8e160]:
                    - strong [ref=f8e161]: Varied Sources
                    - text: ": Ingests both unstructured text and structured data."
                - heading "Getting Started" [level=1] [ref=f8e162]
                - paragraph [ref=f8e163]:
                  - text: "Graphiti is open-source and available on GitHub:"
                  - link "https://git.new/graphiti" [ref=f8e164]:
                    - /url: https://git.new/graphiti
                - paragraph [ref=f8e165]:
                  - text: "Quick Start:"
                  - code [ref=f8e166]: "`pip install graphiti-core`"
                - paragraph [ref=f8e167]: "While we developed Graphiti for our needs at Zep, we believe it could be useful for any application dealing with evolving, interconnected data, such as:"
                - list [ref=f8e168]:
                  - listitem [ref=f8e169]: Personal AI assistants that need to maintain user context over time
                  - listitem [ref=f8e170]: Knowledge management systems for rapidly changing domains
                  - listitem [ref=f8e171]: Social network analysis tools
                  - listitem [ref=f8e172]: Financial systems tracking changing relationships and transactions
                - paragraph [ref=f8e173]: If you try, we'd love to hear your thoughts, questions, and experiences. Please also consider contributing!

        - generic [ref=f7e93]: "Artisan builds AI employees for revenue teams. Our first, Ava, is the leading AI BDR: she finds and researches leads across a database of 400M+ contacts, writes and sends personalized email in your tone of voice, runs dialer call steps, handles every reply, and books meetings on the right rep's calendar. Over 90% of our customers run her fully autonomously. Artisan is a complete GTM ecosystem, not a point tool. One platform consolidates the 5-8 tool stack most teams stitch together at $100K+/year: prospecting data and waterfall enrichment (ZoomInfo, Apollo), list building and signals (Clay), sequencing (Outreach, Salesloft), parallel dialing (Nooks, Orum), website visitor identification, and buyer intent. It runs on top of Salesforce and HubSpot with owner mapping, do-not-contact enforcement, and field-level sync controls. We're built for enterprise. SOC 2 Type II, GDPR and CCPA compliant, SSO/SAML, role-based access, workspace isolation per brand, and a full audit trail on everything Ava does. The common enterprise pattern: sales ops runs Ava centrally for a thousand-plus AEs who never log in. Beyond the BDR job, Ava Inbound qualifies and books website visitors from the same knowledge base, and our AI AE runs live product demos and progresses deals. Prospecting, inbound, and the demo on one platform, one knowledge base, one AI sales team. YC W24. $35M+ raised from investors including Y Combinator and HubSpot Ventures. Thousands of customers including DoorDash, Quora, SumUp, CookUnity and SaaStr. Raise sourced over $700K in ARR in six months with Ava. SumUp runs leads at $52 each. Teams in San Francisco and New York. And we're hiring."

                  - text: Hey! We're Paul, Preston, and Daniel from Zep AI. We've just

                                - link "Zep AI" [ref=f9e22] [cursor=pointer]:

                              - generic [ref=f9e24]:
                                - button [ref=f9e25] [cursor=pointer]

                                - generic [ref=f9e43]: Watch on
                - paragraph [ref=f8e135]:
                  - text: Graphiti helps you create and query graphs that evolve over time. Think of a knowledge graph as a network of interconnected facts, such as
                  - emphasis [ref=f8e136]: “Kendra loves Adidas shoes.”
                  - text: Each fact is a “triplet, represented by two entities, or nodes (
                  - emphasis [ref=f8e137]: ”Kendra,” “Adidas shoes”
                  - text: ), and their relationship, or edge (
                  - emphasis [ref=f8e138]: ”loves”
                  - text: ). Knowledge Graphs have been explored extensively for information retrieval. What makes Graphiti unique is its ability to autonomously build a knowledge graph while handling changing relationships and maintaining historical context.
                - paragraph [ref=f8e139]:
                  - text: At Zep, we build a
                  - link "memory layer for LLM applications" [ref=f8e140]:
                    - /url: https://www.getzep.com
                  - text: . Developers use Zep to recall relevant user information from past conversations without including the entire chat history in a prompt. Accurate context is crucial for LLM applications. If an AI agent doesn't remember that you've changed jobs or confuses the chronology of events, its responses can be jarring or irrelevant, or worse, inaccurate.
                - heading "Zep’s Suboptimal Fact Pipeline" [level=1] [ref=f8e141]
                - paragraph [ref=f8e142]: Before Graphiti, our approach to storing and retrieving user “memory” was, in effect, a specialized RAG pipeline. An LLM extracted “facts” from a user’s chat history. Semantic search, reranking, and other techniques then surfaced facts relevant to the current conversation back to a developer for inclusion in their prompt.
                - paragraph [ref=f8e143]: Unfortunately, this approach became problematic. Reconciling facts from increasingly complex conversations challenged even frontier LLMs such as gpt-4o. We saw incomplete facts, poor recall, and hallucinations. Our RAG search also failed at times to capture the nuanced relationships between facts, leading to irrelevant or contradictory information being retrieved.
                - paragraph [ref=f8e144]: We tried fixing these issues with prompt optimization but saw diminishing returns on effort. We realized that a graph would help model a user’s complex world, potentially addressing these challenges.
                - heading "Building Graphiti" [level=1] [ref=f8e145]
                - paragraph [ref=f8e146]: "We were intrigued by Microsoft’s GraphRAG, which expanded on RAG text chunking with a graph to better model a document corpus. However, it didn't solve our core problem: GraphRAG is designed for static documents and doesn't natively handle temporality."
                - paragraph [ref=f8e147]:
                  - img "uploaded image" [ref=f8e148]
                - paragraph [ref=f8e149]:
                  - text: So, we built Graphiti, a
                  - link "temporal Knowledge Graph" [ref=f8e150]:
                    - /url: https://github.com/getzep/graphiti
                  - text: "library, which is designed from the ground up to handle constantly changing information, hybrid semantic and graph search, and scale:"
                - list [ref=f8e151]:
                  - listitem [ref=f8e152]:
                    - strong [ref=f8e153]: Temporal Awareness
                    - text: ": Tracks changes in facts and relationships over time. Graph edges include temporal metadata to record relationship lifecycles."
                  - listitem [ref=f8e154]:
                    - strong [ref=f8e155]: Episodic Processing
                    - text: ": Ingests data as discrete episodes, maintaining data provenance and enabling incremental processing."
                  - listitem [ref=f8e156]:
                    - strong [ref=f8e157]: Hybrid Search
                    - text: ": Semantic and BM25 full-text search, with the ability to rerank results by distance from a central node."
                  - listitem [ref=f8e158]:
                    - strong [ref=f8e159]: Scalable
                    - text: ": Designed for large datasets, parallelizing LLM calls for batch processing while preserving event chronology."
                  - listitem [ref=f8e160]:
                    - strong [ref=f8e161]: Varied Sources
                    - text: ": Ingests both unstructured text and structured data."
                - heading "Getting Started" [level=1] [ref=f8e162]
                - paragraph [ref=f8e163]:
                  - text: "Graphiti is open-source and available on GitHub:"
                  - link "https://git.new/graphiti" [ref=f8e164]:
                    - /url: https://git.new/graphiti
                - paragraph [ref=f8e165]:
                  - text: "Quick Start:"
                  - code [ref=f8e166]: "`pip install graphiti-core`"
                - paragraph [ref=f8e167]: "While we developed Graphiti for our needs at Zep, we believe it could be useful for any application dealing with evolving, interconnected data, such as:"
                - list [ref=f8e168]:
                  - listitem [ref=f8e169]: Personal AI assistants that need to maintain user context over time
                  - listitem [ref=f8e170]: Knowledge management systems for rapidly changing domains
                  - listitem [ref=f8e171]: Social network analysis tools
                  - listitem [ref=f8e172]: Financial systems tracking changing relationships and transactions
                - paragraph [ref=f8e173]: If you try, we'd love to hear your thoughts, questions, and experiences. Please also consider contributing!
